text: Day two. And India hits you with a problem nobody warns you about. You need to pay someone. Your UPI app is in the drawer. You need a train ticket. Almost nine out of ten reserved tickets are now booked online. You're in a new part of the city. No maps. No idea where you are. Then your bank sends an O T P... to a phone you can't touch. {playful} So you walk into a mobile shop and buy the one phone that can't scroll. An old keypad phone. Calls and S M S. That's it. {neutral} But now you see it. Your phone was never just a phone. It's your wallet, your ticket counter, your map and your bank. So you carry cash. You ask strangers for directions. Like it's two thousand five.
